situation:
You are to assume the role of client services coordinator at PIKE HOLLOW TECHNOLOGY CO-OPERATIVE, an information technology services provider owned by the forty people who work in it. The co-operative installs and supports point-of-sale and inventory systems for retail stores across the region. The general manager (judge), elected by the member-owners, has asked to meet with you.

EASTGATE MARKETS, the co-operative's largest customer, has asked for the full hour-by-hour demand figures the co-operative has gathered from every retail account it serves. Eastgate would use them to plan its holiday merchandising and its shelf displays. Those figures carry the selling peaks and the stock settings of two smaller retailers who compete directly with Eastgate.

Every service agreement the co-operative signs carries a confidentiality clause, and the two smaller retailers gave their numbers under it. Releasing the combined demand figures to Eastgate would break that clause and could cost the co-operative the business of both smaller retailers. Sending Eastgate only the co-operative's own totals, with no customer named, risks the reply that the totals are too vague to plan holiday displays.

Eastgate has hinted that it would move its contract to a larger vendor at renewal. The general manager (judge) wants your recommendation on what the co-operative sends Eastgate and how that answer is explained to the customer. The general manager (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of the general manager at PIKE HOLLOW TECHNOLOGY CO-OPERATIVE, elected to the post by the member-owners. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have asked the participant to recommend what the co-operative sends EASTGATE MARKETS in answer to its request for the demand figures, and how that answer is explained to the customer.

The participant will present their recommendation to you in a role-play to take place in your office. You will begin the role-play by greeting the participant and asking to hear their ideas.

During the role-play, you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us the two smaller retailers still trust us?
